channel.title: Lecture Notes on MIT OpenCourseWare
channel.description: Recent content in Lecture Notes on MIT OpenCourseWare

item.title: Inertial Instruments and Inertial Navigation
item.description: Lecture notes on inertial instruments and inertial navigation, gimbals, gyros, inertial platforms, accelerometers, and aircraft and spacecraft system applications of inertial systems.

item.title: Lecture L1 – Introduction
item.description: Lecture notes with an overview of the course and introduction to dynamics.

item.title: Lecture L10 – Angular Impulse and Momentum for a Particle
item.description: Lecture notes on the angular impulse and momentum for a particle.

item.title: Lecture L11 – Conservation Laws for Systems of Particles
item.description: Lecture notes on conservation laws for systems of particles, Newton’s second law, conservation of angular momentum, and two-dimensional rigid bodies.

item.title: Lecture L12 – Work and Energy
item.description: Lecture notes on mechanical work, the principle of work and energy, external and internal forces, and power.

item.title: Lecture L13 – Conservative Internal Forces and Potential Energy
item.description: Lecture notes on conservative internal forces, conservation of energy, equilibrium and stability, and potential energy.

item.title: Lecture L14 – Variable Mass Systems: The Rocket Equation
item.description: Lecture notes on variable mass systems and the rocket equation.

item.title: Lecture L15 – Central Force Motion: Kepler's Laws
item.description: Lecture notes on central force motion, Kepler’s laws, Newton’s second law, equations of motion, and elliptical trajectories.

item.title: Lecture L16 – Central Force Motion: Orbits
item.description: Lecture notes on central force motion, orbits, conservation of energy, and trajectories.

item.title: Lecture L17 – Orbit Transfers and Interplanetary Trajectories
item.description: Lecture notes on orbit transfers and interplanetary trajectories.

item.title: Lecture L18 – Exploring the Neighborhood: the Restricted Three-Body Problem
item.description: Lecture notes on the three-body problem, stability, and application of the Lagrange Points.

item.title: Lecture L19 – Vibration, Normal Modes, Natural Frequencies, Instability
item.description: Lecture notes on vibration, normal modes,natural frequencies, and instability.

item.title: Lecture L2 – Degrees of Freedom and Constraints, Rectilinear Motion
item.description: Lecture notes on degrees of freedom, constraints, and rectilinear motion.

item.title: Lecture L20 – Energy Methods: Lagrange’s Equations
item.description: Lecture notes on derivation of Lagrange’s equations in Cartesian coordinates, extension to general coordinate systems, simple pendulum by Lagrange’s equations, double pendulum by Lagrange’s equations, and derivation of Lagrange’s equation for general coordinate systems.

item.title: Lecture L21 – 2D Rigid Body Dynamics
item.description: Lecture notes on 2D rigid body dynamics.

item.title: Lecture L22 – 2D Rigid Body Dynamics: Work and Energy
item.description: Lecture notes on 2D rigid body dynamics, work, and energy.

item.title: Lecture L23 – 2D Rigid Body Dynamics: Impulse and Momentum
item.description: Lecture notes on two dimensional rigid body dynamics, impulse and momentum equations, and the center of percussion relative to an instantaneous center of motion.

item.title: Lecture L24 – Pendulums
item.description: Lecture notes on simple pendulum and compound pendulums, the center of percussion, reversibility, the Kater pendulum, and the Schuler pendulum.

item.title: Lecture L25 – 3D Rigid Body Kinematics
item.description: Lecture notes on 3D rigid body kinematics, rotation about a fixed point, angular velocity about a fixed point, angular acceleration, instantaneous axis of rotation, and general motion.

item.title: Lecture L26 – 3D Rigid Body Dynamics: The Inertia Tensor
item.description: Lecture notes on 3D rigid body dynamics and the inertia tensor.

item.title: Lecture L27 – 3D Rigid Body Dynamics: Kinetic Energy; Instability; Equations of Motion
item.description: Lecture notes on 3D rigid body dynamics, kinetic energy for systems of particles, and governing equations for rotational motion of a three-dimensional body.

item.title: Lecture L28 – 3D Rigid Body Dynamics: Equations of Motion; Euler’s Equations
item.description: Lecture notes on 3D rigid body dynamics, equations of motion, and Euler’s equations.

item.title: Lecture L29 – 3D Rigid Body Dynamics
item.description: Lecture notes on 3D rigid body dynamics, Euler angles, free motions of a rotating body, and extreme aircraft dynamics.

item.title: Lecture L3 – Vectors, Matrices and Coordinate Transformations
item.description: Lecture notes on vectors, matrices, and coordinate transformations.

item.title: Lecture L30 – 3D Rigid Body Dynamics: Tops and Gyroscopes
item.description: Lecture notes on 3D rigid body dynamics, Euler’s equations, steady precession, gyroscopic motion, unsteady precession of a top, and integrals of motion.

item.title: Lecture L4 – Curvilinear Motion. Cartesian Coordinates
item.description: Lecture notes on curvilinear motion and Cartesian coordinates.

item.title: Lecture L5 – Other Coordinate Systems
item.description: Lecture notes on polar coordinates in two dimensions and cylindrical and spherical coordinates in three dimensions.

item.title: Lecture L6 – Intrinsic Coordinates
item.description: Lecture notes on intrinsic coordinate systems, tangential, normal and binormal components, and equations of motion in intrinsic coordinates.

item.title: Lecture L7 – Relative Motion using Translating Axes
item.description: Lecture notes on relative motion using translating axes.

item.title: Lecture L8 – Relative Motion using Rotating Axes
item.description: Lecture notes on relative motion on rotating axes, Time derivative of a fixed vector in a rotating frame, Coriolis’ theorem, and Relationships between position, and velocity and acceleration vectors from rotating to non-rotating coordinate systems.

item.title: Lecture L9 – Linear Impulse and Momentum. Collisions
item.description: Lecture notes on the principle of linear impulse and momentum, and collisions.

item.title: Some Dynamics and Control Challenges that occurred during the Apollo Project
item.description: Lecture presentation on dynamics and control challenges that occurred during the Apollo project.
